Once again we had a "make-weight" team in the 4 x 300 yards, this time Sid Ring and Cecil Penny turned out for us, and the result was the same as for the hundreds. We had first three home in the 1 Mile Team, our men being Allum, A.
Frank Webb ran very well for us in this, and Henderson, of the Poly, only beat him by a yard or so, over the half-mile stage. A.
Trapnell aslo broke a ground record when winning the Mile race in 4 min. 28 sec. and A.
In the Mile he set up a new record time of 4 min. 30 sec. and beat a good-sized field which included most of our best distance men. Pat Parker was second, with A.

Cohen's effort was a very fine one, and we now seemed well set for our fourth victory. A.
Pat Parker turned out for us in the Mile and won in easy fashion, with A.
About two miles out we came across a miniature Everest which we had to climb, and what a climb! A.

Harry Shields went off next and battled his way round to hand over in third position to Tommy Morrell, who was our next runner. Tom ran very well indeed and took us up a place so that Alf. Shaw was sent off in second place, and with Les.
Result:— 1 Dockerill (D) 27.35; 2 L Cohen, 27.46; 4 H. Shields, 28.24; 5 A.

Stan Blunden ran well to win the 220 Yards, and our representatives for the 440 were Alf Shaw and Les Cohen! George Powell had a field day in winning three field events, while young Hendry showed the results of Charlie Jones' careful coaching in clearing his highest jump of the season.
